subject: Request: temporary backup purge standstill + DPA / subprocessor list
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@brightwellhealth.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request to pause backup purge while DPA redline is in review

Hi David,

Quick note from Brightwell's legal and M&A teams — we're in the final stages of an acquisition and need a short-term assurance that any scheduled backup purges that could remove customer data will be paused while our legal team completes a DPA addendum and subprocessor review.

Specific asks:
- Can Redwood put a temporary hold on any scheduled backup/snapshot purges that would affect Brightwell data for 90 days?
- We need an up-to-date subprocessor list and the last SOC2 attestations for each subprocessor that handles backups or telemetry.
- If there are immutable snapshots or escrow procedures in place, please confirm how they interact with a hold request.

Attachments: security questionnaire (completed) and our proposed DPA redlines.

This is time-sensitive for our board; please let us know who on your side should be looped in for legal/ops coordination.

Thanks,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Privacy & Compliance | Brightwell Health
[marta.ruiz@brightwellhealth.com]
[Attachment: Brightwell_Security_Questionnaire_v2.pdf (application/pdf)]
[Attachment: DPA_redline_Brightwell.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@brightwellhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request to pause backup purge while DPA redline is in review

Marta — thanks for the heads up and the questionnaire. I'll own coordination on our side.

Quick replies / next steps from Redwood:
- I've looped Legal (Kimberly) and Ops (Laura). Kimberly — can you confirm the DPA amendment path and whether a 90-day hold is acceptable operationally from a contract standpoint?
- Laura — can you enumerate which backup classes/snapshots cover Brightwell (hot backups, offsite snapshots, immutable escrow) and the current purge schedule? We need a short technical manifest so we can scope the hold precisely.
- Ben — I'll need you to own the external communications cadence with Brightwell and set expectations on timing.

For Brightwell: an initial operating assumption from our side is that we can gate the scheduled purge for customer-scoped snapshots for a temporary period, but the specific mechanics depend on what gets held (short-term ephemeral caches vs. long-term snapshots vs. escrow).

I propose we start with a 60-day operational hold while Legal expedites the DPA addendum; if Brightwell prefers 90 days we can escalate to execs for approval. Please confirm which timeline you'd prefer and we'll escalate internally if needed.

-David
David Kim
Director, Account Strategy | Redwood Inference
[david.kim@redwood.com]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@brightwellhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 10:24:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request to pause backup purge while DPA redline is in review

David / team — legal perspective below.

1) DPA amendment path: we can offer an addendum that temporarily extends retention/hold terms for Brightwell while preserving our standard liability and transfer clauses. We'll need the redlines from Brightwell's counsel (we have them attached) and 1–2 business days to prepare our counter. DocuSign route preferred for speed.

2) Timeline suggestion: operationally 60 days is our default for temporary holds (limits operational risk and audit impact). If Brightwell needs 90 days, Legal will require an explicit exec-level approval and a narrow scoped clause (customer-specific hold; automatic expiry unless extended).

3) Subprocessor list & attestations: Ops must provide a list of subprocessors that store or process backups (including cloud provider archive buckets, managed snapshot agents, and any long-term escrow partner). For each subprocessor we need: name, location of processing, last SOC2/ISO attestation date, and whether encrypted-at-rest keys are client-controlled.

4) Evidence package: once Ops provides the manifest, Security will produce an evidence pack (audit logs showing backup retention, last access, and purge schedule) that Brightwell can use in diligence.

Action items assigned:
- Laura: provide subprocessor manifest + backup/snapshot mapping by EOD Wed 2026-12-02.
- Ben: prepare customer communications template (friendly but firm on conditionality).
- David: coordinate exec escalation if Brightwell insists on 90 days.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
[kimberly.park@redwood.com]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@brightwellhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request to pause backup purge while DPA redline is in review

Thanks — manifest and technical details below (summary). I attached a CSV manifest and a short subprocessor spreadsheet for legal review.

Backup classes that could be in scope:
- Hot instance snapshots (S3 snapshots + KV snapshot exports) — default purge cadence: 30d -> 90d (tiered), scheduled purge job: 2027-01-15 02:00 UTC.
- Offsite archival snapshots (glacier-type) — retention 365d; purge window: quarterly; immutable escrow: third-party escrow provider (EscrowSafe) holds a single immutable vault for legal holds.
- Telemetry & ephemeral logs — TTL 7d (no change), not included in long-term backups.
- Audit trail logs (security/audit) — retained 365d in our analytics lake; we can provide evidence extracts but cannot permanently change global retention without exec approval.

Subprocessors included in manifest:
- CloudArchiveCo (S3-like storage) — SOC2 2026-06-15, EU/US regions.
- EscrowSafe (escrow provider) — ISO27001 2025-11-01, holds immutable snapshots when escrow workflow invoked.
- SnapshotAgent Inc. (managed snapshot orchestration) — SOC2 2026-02-09.

Operational approach we recommend:
- Implement a scoped hold flag for Brightwell on their backup objects and on queued purge jobs. This prevents the scheduled purge job on 2027-01-15 from removing customer-scoped snapshots.
- For immutable escrow items, mark Brightwell's vault objects as "hold: true" at the escrow provider (EscrowSafe requires a signed DPA addendum and an API ticket to flip the hold state).
- Logs: we can extract and provide audit evidence for the period in question but cannot alter core analytics retention without approval.

Proposed timeline (operational):
- EOD 2026-12-02: Redwood provides manifest + attachments (attached).
- 2026-12-03 to 2026-12-10: Legal and Brightwell finalize redlines via DocuSign.
- If DPA addendum signed by 2026-12-10: we set the hold immediately and block purge scheduled for 2027-01-15.
- Default hold window: 60 days from hold start (if Brightwell needs longer, escalate).

Attachments (sent): backup_manifest_Brightwell_20261202.csv, subprocessors_brightwell_20261202.xlsx

Laura Bennett
Director, Platform Operations | Redwood Inference
